pr_title: Allow no tabs to be selected in TabBar and TabContainer
pr_body:
- closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8233
- related #21223
- fixes #74653
- fixes #73785
- fixes `remove_tab()` and `move_tabs()` not updating previous tab properly.
- related: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/50930#issuecomment-1782019598

When TabContainer children visibility changes, that tab is marked as current and other tabs are deselected.

Adds deselect_enabled property to TabBar and TabContainer so that no tabs can be selected (disabled by default).
current_tab can now be -1 if this is enabled or there are no valid tabs.

Considerations:
- If there is only one child of a TabContainer and deselect_enabled is false, then the child cannot be hidden.
- This also prevents multiple TabContainer children from being visible at once.
- Changing visibility of TabContainer children changes the current tab, so when editing you need to make sure to switch to the tab you want to be the first selected tab before saving the scene.
pr_comments:
How does this fix https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/21223?

Also there is some bug when adding a first child to a newly created TabContainer. The child is invisible and you can't make it appear by changing current tab.

Oh, I misread #21223, this only address the 'bonus' part of it, where clicking the eye to change visibility sets the current tab and the others are hidden. Changed to just be related.

~And I think the invisible child issue is partly because I changed how the tab_changed signal fires in edge cases, but maybe I shouldn't change it for compatibility.~
When adding the first tab to a TabBar, should the tab_changed signal be emitted when it is added out of the tree? TabContainer does but TabBar doesn't.

Edit: Fixed the issue, the default current tab when there are no tabs is now -1. If there are any tabs added it will be changed to 0.

Since tab deselection is disabled by default as well, the current tab is automatically changed to 0 if there are any tabs when the scene loads (in editor or not), so there should be no change in behavior.

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/10054226/6c81d994-ded8-45bc-ac23-e7824cf1ec32)

> The logic for setting -1 can be improved. Pseudocode:

This would change the logic. All tabs must be hidden or disabled for deselection, not any.
I can add the condition and change it to a for each loop though.

Right, I updated it.
EDIT:
Nevermind, I think it's still wrong. Yeah you can go with your code.

Fixed issue when removing all but a disabled tab would deselect that tab instead of none.
Fixed multiple tab_changed signals when moving tab.

I added an MRP to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/74653 with steps.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/73785 is a duplicate of it.

So your PR adds tab changing based on visibility 🤔
Well, can't say if it's expected/desirable, but at least it works correctly.
When no tab is selected, the panel itself isn't draw. This shouldn't be how it works.

> When no tab is selected, the panel itself isn't draw. This shouldn't be how it works.

This is intended, because I am planning to make the Editor's Bottom Dock into a TabContainer, and the Panel will need to hide.
I could add an option for it if we want?
Then the "panel" theme style should be overridden with an empty one instead.
Why would we want to draw the panel if there is no content to display?

- It's already the default behavior to always show the panel, even if there's no tabs available.
- It's visually displeasing to have the panel completely vanish while the tabs are still hanging in there.
- The panel can still be used to display some sort of content by the user, depending on their needs.

> * It's already the default behavior to always show the panel, even if there's no tabs available.
> * It's visually displeasing to have the panel completely vanish while the tabs are still hanging in there.

This is rather arbitrary. The default behavior doesn't change anyway, and if you enable the feature to allow closing all the tabs, then you want to be able to close all tabs, not just hide their content.

> * The panel can still be used to display some sort of content by the user, depending on their needs.

This is hard to control, so it would be limited in its usefulness. However, it got me thinking. We have `use_hidden_tabs_for_min_size`, which is not respected in this case. But it should. We should still draw the panel at least if we enable this option.

Edit: Which... may still be not what you want if you want to close all the tabs, but display them all at the same minimum size once they are visible? Eh, I don't know.

> This is rather arbitrary. The default behavior doesn't change anyway, and if you enable the feature to allow closing all the tabs, then you want to be able to close all tabs, not just hide their content.

I meant that the default behavior is to present the panel regardless of tab state (as even if there's no children, the panel will still be there), because that's the whole point of `TabContainer`. Otherwise, one might as well just use `TabBar`.

> This is hard to control, so it would be limited in its usefulness.

Still less of a niche case than not wanting to see the panel, which is easily solvable by just placing an empty `StyleBox` in the "panel" style.

I changed it to draw the panel when no tabs are selected.
Since I'm not using `use_hidden_tabs_for_min_size`, the panel will collapse away for me anyway.
Setting the panel style to empty is good for other use-cases I was thinking of too.
If a user wants it to collapse while using `use_hidden_tabs_for_min_size`, they could toggle it off when they get a `-1` tab_changed signal.

issue_context.title: Godot 4 rc3: TabBar child node set anchor not working in the editor.
issue_context.body: ### Godot version v4.0.rc3.official (7e79aea) ### System information Mac Air M1 2020 ### Issue description TabBar childs anchor not working in editor. ### Steps to reproduce Create a TabContainer node with some Tabbar node inside it. Then create some UI node inside Tabbar node. Set any anchor to child node, nothing happen. The child still in Vector2.ZERO. Note: only child on first Tabbar node works. ### Minimal reproduction project [Uploading GodotProject.zip…]()
comments: TabContainer already contains a TabBar. What are you trying to do?

> TabContainer already contains a TabBar. What are you trying to do?

i mean when i create content inside tabbar, i can't set anchor to it. For example when I create a button, i can't set it center or full rect to it. Everything is still normal when on godot 3.5.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57259604/221079765-866723bb-fe98-4953-9854-32c1e5819045.mp4

My question is why are you adding extra tabbars to the TabContainer, when TabContainer already has a tabbar, and you don't need to add one yourself. Tabs will be created automatically once you add any control node child to the TabContainer. So what are you trying to achieve by adding extra tabbar nodes?
For multiple tabs, of course. Even so, still have a bit of a problem with setting anchor to it. Especially in ui interface design.

@dqdthanhthanh You don't need to add `TabBar` to `TabContainer`. Tabs are created from child control nodes, like `PanelContainer`, or `MarginContainer`, or one of the box containers. `TabContainer` already has a tabbar, it's built-in.

Same is true for 3.x, where I assume you use the `Tabs` nodes as children of `TabContainer`. This is incorrect and not needed. We specifically renamed the `Tabs` node to `TabBar` to indicate that it's a representation of the tabbar itself, not a special "tab" node (as there is no such thing in Godot). Any child control of `TabContainer` becomes a tab in it. The tabbar is built-in.

Thanks. But I mean set anchor for node sometimes doesn't work. For example button node (video from 15 seconds)


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57259604/221209504-f28ff7ee-0357-40e0-a73b-3b1e824de299.mp4

Plain Control nodes don't have any size, and don't grow in size to fit their children. So your second and third tabs have no side. Anchoring works correctly, as far as I can see, because controls have no size and are displayed from top-left. You want to use containers there not plain controls and anchors.

That's what I mean, in the first node the size is equal to the screen ratio and easyly set anchor. The remaining nodes are size = (0,0) and cannot be edit. So I don't know if it's a bug or not. Or am I doing it wrong way?
![123](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57259604/221218283-c7476b0c-706d-4b25-a73f-81e4b9665e18.JPG)
![Capture](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57259604/221216908-21fce849-0ba1-4ff5-8c76-d09a3fcb1802.JPG)
[](url)
Yes, you aren't using containers where you should. And you also need to set min size, not just size, as containers will override the size (and position) as that is their function.
